title: AI Daytrading, is it real?
author: melasturdo
selftext: I keep seeing, all over tiktok, people who day trade using ai, where the stock is moving super fast and there seems to be something selling and buying at the perfect times (photo 1) , other times, there is an overlay that just tells you when to buy or when to sell which seems only semi accurate in the second photo, but other times I see it predicting perfectly, is this legit?

comments.author: liuhaolin911
comments.body: Do you think outsource the brain to AI a good idea?

comments.author: Scott_Malkinsons
comments.body:
That's just mapping standard deviations, it's a fancy Bollinger Band.

Keep in mind John Bollinger is still alive, and he's basically broke as balls. He made the indicator in like the 80's so he could sell VHS tapes with courses. These days he makes most his money suing people who use the Bollinger Band trademark while he works out of a shitty office on Aviation Blvd that I pass on the way to the W6TRW swap meet. Working across from an abandoned 99 cent store and a Jack in a Box with bars to protect the cashiers does not scream good profitable trading product.

The reason it looks all perfect is because it adapts on every bar (that's why the high and low changes so often). It was designed to look good, to sell sources, not to make money. If it made money, John Bollinger would be a lot richer.

... and it's not AI in the first place, it's literally Bollinger Bands.

comments.author: Air_Original
comments.body: Take a ruler. Line it up with the buy/sell signals and their respective candles. Those are lagging indications, which means that the signal appears after the candle closes. Imagine a buy signal appearing after a huge green candle or a sell signal after a knife candle.
